iut_type: Development prototype (BLE module embedded in a coupling component, Miki Pulley)
customer_question: If the 'free evaluation equipment loan' itself remains unpaid, but we charge separately for the engineer dispatch fee needed to set up the equipment on-site, can we still consider SIG certification unnecessary?
question_variants: Can we charge for engineer support/installation while keeping the device loan itself free, and still avoid SIG certification?
Does charging for technical support services (separate from the device) break the free-loan exemption?
actual_issue: Miki Pulley wanted to charge for dispatching technicians to install/set up the evaluation equipment on customer sites (since expertise is required), while keeping the loan of the Bluetooth-equipped device itself free, and asked whether this still avoided SIG certification.
plain_english_explanation: As long as no payment is requested for the Bluetooth-enabled device itself, charging separately for an engineer support/dispatch service does not break the free-loan exemption. The certification requirement is tied to compensation for the Bluetooth device, not for adjacent services.
consultant_answer: If no payment is required for the Bluetooth device itself, but the engineer support dispatch is positioned and billed as a separate paid service, then SIG certification of the evaluation equipment is not mandatory.
decision_logic: The exemption hinges narrowly on whether the Bluetooth product itself is exchanged for money. Bundling a paid professional service alongside a free device loan does not, by itself, convert the device loan into a commercial transaction.
final_recommendation: If structuring a hybrid free-device/paid-service offering, clearly separate the device loan agreement (free) from the service agreement (paid) in contracts and invoicing to preserve the exemption.
risk_if_done_wrong: If the cost structure conflates the device loan and the service fee (e.g., a single bundled price that implicitly compensates for device use), the exemption could be challenged.
